articles.summary: Direct-detection optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM) suits hybrid fibre–free-space-optical (FSO) links because simple per-subcarrier equalisation tolerates chromatic dispersion and turbulence, but its peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) drives the Mach–Zehnder modulator into nonlinearity and degrades bit-error rate (BER). This Monte Carlo study compares clipping and filtering, μ-law companding, selected mapping (SLM) and a hybrid SLM + μ-law scheme for 16-QAM DCO-OFDM over single-mode fibre cascaded with a Gamma–Gamma turbulence channel. SLM + μ-law gives the largest PAPR reduction, from 13.50 dB to 7.83 dB at 10 −3 , yet PAPR alone does not predict link performance. …

Owing to the interplay between the radially polarized correlation structure and the vortex phase, the beam exhibits an unusual intensity evolution during propagation, with its focal-field profile tunable by the topological charge. …

articles.summary: Optical skyrmions provide a vital platform for integrating quasiparticle physics, topological theory, and advanced electromagnetic control. Traditionally, the helicity of their topological textures exhibits central symmetry, restricting them to purely Néel or Bloch types. Here, we propose a novel class─optical Janus skyrmions─featuring spatial symmetry breaking of helicity, where Néel and Bloch types spatially coexist in a double-sided heterogeneous configuration. We experimentally generate Janus skyrmions in structured light beams. …

However, current all‐optical switching approaches cannot simultaneously shape the output wavefront, because combining pixelated phase control with high‐Q nanostructures remains extremely challenging. Here, we demonstrate picosecond all‐optical switching of the unpolarized incident light with engineered output wavefronts via nonlocal geometric‐phase gradient metasurfaces supporting high‐Q chiral quasi‐bound states in the continuum (quasi‐BICs). …

articles.summary: Chirality is a fundamental asymmetry in nature. In optics, control of chirality is evolving from spatial properties like polarization to the temporal chirality of local fields. Conventional approaches, however, encode chirality in abstract degrees of freedom such as phase or polarization, limiting direct and efficient coupling with matter on ultrafast timescales. We introduce and experimentally demonstrate a paradigm of intensity-driven optical chirality, where handedness is physically inscribed into the trajectory of spatiotemporal energy flow. Through the engineered non-collinear collision of Spatiotemporal Optical Vortices, the spatiotemporal optical coil is generated. …

While metasurfaces have emerged as powerful approaches for dynamic holography, existing works remain largely confined to intensity-only modulation, restricting the available channels for display and information storage. Herein, we realize a generalized platform applicable to major types of dynamic holography (monochromatic, color, 3D, and vectorial) by introducing a learned metasurface and aperture synthesis framework (LMAS). …

articles.title: Measurement of rotation angle variation using conjugate vortex beams
articles.authors: Bohao Chen, Jiadian Yan, Jun Yao, Lu Peng, Zixian Ma, Xuanbin Chen, Zhi‐Han Zhu, Yuanjie Yang

articles.summary: The measurement of rotation angle variations is crucial in advanced manufacturing and precision sciences. However, conventional optical methods are fundamentally restricted by the pixel size of camera arrays used to resolve spatial interference patterns. To address this limitation, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate a pixel-independent measurement scheme based on matched filtering of conjugate vortex beams. This approach directly transforms rotation angle variations into periodic oscillations of the central intensity. Decoding is achieved simply by counting intensity extrema, eliminating the dependence on camera pixel resolution for angular decoding. …

articles.summary: We study how the topological properties of a one-dimensional staggered lattice, loaded into states with orbital angular momentum l=1, can be controlled simply by tuning the relative angle between sites. The original system under consideration can be depicted as a Creutz ladder model when unwrapping the different state circulations in a synthetic dimension. Depending on the hopping strengths of the chain, different topological regimes may be accessed by changing the ladder angle, as determined by the value of the winding number of the chain. …

articles.summary: A confined compressible jet can undergo aerodynamic instability through coupled shear-layer amplification, wave forcing, and pressure-wave redistribution. Conventional single-point pressure spectra cannot distinguish spatial organization from propagation, limiting mechanistic diagnosis. This study combines pressure-array wavenumber-frequency (k − f) spectra with large-eddy-simulation diagnostics to examine operating-condition-dependent spectral reorganization in a generic compressible-gas Laval-tube special valve. Each condition uses a 20-cycle pressure record. The typical and 363.15 K low-frequency conditions each include three independent seed-perturbed realizations. …

articles.summary: Coherent single-pixel imaging (CSPI) enables amplitude- and phase-resolved computational imaging with a single coherent detector, offering particular advantages in spectral regimes where high-performance detector arrays remain unavailable. In conventional Fourier-plane CSPI, the detector is typically placed at the focal point to maximize the collected power. However, this focal position does not necessarily maximize the reconstruction fidelity for image reconstruction in the presence of system nonidealities. Here, we introduce detector position as an additional degree of freedom for CSPI optimization. …

articles.authors: Shunpei Nara, Hayato Kobayashi, Kousuke Kusano, Yuta Takai, Hiroyuki Kowa, Toshitaka Wakayama, Takeshi Higashiguchi
articles.summary: The polarization state of a supercontinuum (SC) vector beam provides a reference for quantitative polarimetry. We characterize an azimuthally polarized SC vector beam generated with an S-waveplate and azimuthal polarizers by wavelength-resolved Stokes imaging. Representative maps show an approximately tangential azimuthal angle and a small ellipticity parameter over much of the beam, together with the degree of polarization. The ± 90° azimuthal angle boundary shifts by about 21° between 450 and 766 nm. A linear fit gives 21° ± 7°, where the uncertainty is derived from the slope confidence interval and does not include uncharacterized systematic errors. …

articles.summary: Optical skyrmions are topologically protected spin textures in structured light, whose continuous and versatile control is central to advancing topological photonics and enabling robust optical functionalities. Here, we establish a universal geometric framework for the continuous transformation of stokes skyrmions via the evolution of orthogonal polarization bases on the Poincaré sphere. We show that basis rotations induce deterministic rotations of local spin vectors across the entire field, enabling a unified description of topological evolution. …

articles.summary: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) dominate visual computing, but their electronic implementations face fundamental bottlenecks in speed and energy efficiency. Although photonic alternatives offer a promising route, all‐optical image recognition using CNNs remains challenging in experiments due to the difficulty of implementing effective weak‐light nonlinearities. Here, we demonstrate a streamlined all‐optical CNN architecture with only physically guided, fixed convolutional and trainable fully‐connected layers (FCLs), which circumvents explicit, energy‐intensive nonlinear layers. …

Recent advances show that metasurface functionalities can be further promoted from performing in only the transmission/reflection space to simultaneously and independently in both spaces. However, related studies so far mostly rely on electromagnetic multiplexing strategies where two intrinsically incident waves are required, i.e., the transmission and reflection functionalities are realized at different electromagnetic parameter conditions. …

articles.summary: Cascaded holographic architectures offer enhanced functionality for optical information processing, encryption, and multiplexing, but their practical implementation is severely limited by extreme sensitivity to interlayer alignment. Here, we demonstrate a dynamic cascaded holography platform using commercial phase‐only spatial light modulators by introducing a robust optimization framework that explicitly incorporates random misalignment errors into the wave propagation model. By optimizing phase patterns over diverse alignment conditions, the resulting holograms maintain stable reconstruction performance under lateral displacements of up to ∼100 pixels. …

Additionally, the merging BIC formed by multiple BICs also lacks a mechanistic non‐Hermitian interpretation, and its implementations are confined to the momentum space of photonic crystal slabs, hindering dynamic modulation. …

articles.summary: Metasurfaces offer versatile platforms for multifunctional electromagnetic‐wave manipulation, yet extending the number and diversity of accessible functions remains challenging because conventional multiplexing schemes rely on independently addressable physical degrees of freedom. Here, we demonstrate a directional‐rotational cascaded (DRC) metasurface in which the electromagnetic response is jointly controlled by propagation direction, relative in‐plane rotation, and incident‐field condition. A single fabricated two‐layer device experimentally realizes ten heterogeneous functions spanning electromagnetic computing, holography, focusing, and vortex‐beam generation. …

articles.authors: Fan‐Chuan Lin, Qian Huang, Yi-Long Li, Rui‐Yi Zhao, Qiong‐Hua Wang, Jianghao Xiong, Di Wang
articles.summary: As a promising 3D display technology, holographic display can reconstruct full light field information of 3D scenes, including depth cues. While depth‐dependent defocus naturally provides these depth cues, the limited depth of focus (DOF) restricts the axial range of image clarity, posing a significant challenge for layer‐based holographic displays. In this work, we innovatively propose a large‐DOF and high‐quality layer‐based holographic 3D display system based on a liquid crystal axicon. The core components of the proposed system include a spatial light modulator (SLM) loaded with high‐quality holograms and a specially designed liquid crystal axicon. …

articles.summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) generates correlated photon pairs that inherently exhibit high-dimensional spatial entanglement in orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes. In practice, the resulting two-photon states are typically not maximally entangled due to a highly non-uniform distribution of generated OAM modes. Although pump-beam engineering has emerged as a tool to prepare high-dimensional entangled states, it has usually been restricted to low-dimensional subspaces, i.e., small sets of selected OAM modes for each photon within the full infinite-dimensional two-photon Hilbert space. …

articles.authors: Shiyi Wu, Andrey Novitsky
articles.journal: Journal of the Optical Society of America B
articles.summary: Optical manipulation provides a powerful means of controlling microscopic particles, and optical pulling is particularly attractive because it enables particle transport against the incident momentum. However, predicting whether a finite multipolar response can support optical pulling remains challenging because the outcome depends jointly on the scattering state and the incident beam. Here, we establish a finite-multipole accessibility framework that provides a formal upper-bound criterion for determining whether optical pulling is excluded or kinematically permitted within a truncated multipolar space. …

articles.summary: Spiral–pinhole arrays offer a simple binary approach to optical vortex generation, especially in spectral regions lacking programmable phase modulators, but conventional designs mainly produce annular beams with limited geometric control. Here, we propose geometric pinhole encoding for flexible synthesis of polygonal vortex beams. A prescribed polygonal contour is mapped onto a nonuniform azimuthal phase with a total circulation of 2 π l , where l is the topological charge, and then encoded into the radial coordinates of discrete pinholes through propagation-induced optical path differences. …

articles.authors: Faorlin T, Panzl L, Grosser P, Viñas P, Kahan A, Hörmann WJ, Weiser Y, Cerchiari G, Feldker T, Erhard A, Jacob G, Ulmanis J, Blatt R, Bermudez A, Monz T
articles.summary: Spectral crowding of collective motional modes limits the fidelity of entangling interactions in trapped-ion quantum processors by inducing off-resonant coupling to spectator modes. We introduce a geometric-phase entangling interaction driven by a transverse, time-dependent structured-light force. By applying the force in a plane orthogonal to the optical propagation direction, we reduce the effects of spectral crowding while preserving single-ion addressing. The scheme is compatible with arbitrary qubit encodings, provided that the qubit states experience a differential AC Stark shift. …
